featured.title: G7 Releases Emergency Oil Stocks as Iran Conflict Keeps Energy Markets Under Pressure
featured.content: The G7 has agreed to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude oil from emergency reserves over four months in an effort to ease pressure on fuel markets. The International Energy Agency will coordinate the release, with a substantial portion of diesel expected to enter markets early in the programme. The decision comes as the Iran conflict and disruption around the Strait of Hormuz continue to affect global energy supplies and refined-product markets.
featured.imageQuery: G7 energy meeting oil barrels emergency reserves

articles.title: US–Iran Crisis Remains Unresolved as Washington Reviews Its Next Move
articles.content: The confrontation between the United States and Iran remains unresolved. President Donald Trump has indicated that Washington is approaching decisions on Iran, while Tehran continues to face severe economic and military pressure. Iran has previously proposed conditions involving a halt to hostilities, sanctions relief and reopening the Strait of Hormuz, but Reuters reports that the diplomatic process remains difficult and no comprehensive settlement has been reached.
articles.imageQuery: Donald Trump Iran diplomacy White House

articles.title: Iraq Moves 2 Million Barrels of Crude Through Strait of Hormuz
articles.content: Iraq's state-owned Oil Tanker Company says it successfully transported 2 million barrels of Iraqi crude through the Strait of Hormuz aboard a very large crude carrier. The company described the operation as its first such transit through the strategic waterway in decades. The development highlights continuing efforts by oil producers to maintain export routes despite security risks.
articles.imageQuery: Iraqi oil tanker Strait of Hormuz

articles.title: G7 Emergency Oil Release Targets Global Fuel Pressure
articles.content: G7 countries have agreed to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude oil from emergency reserves over four months. The International Energy Agency is coordinating the operation, with a significant portion of diesel expected to be released during the first 20 days. The measure is intended to increase market liquidity and reduce pressure on fuel prices following supply disruptions linked to the Middle East conflict.
articles.imageQuery: oil storage tanks energy reserves fuel market

articles.title: France Faces Escalating Student Protests
articles.content: Student protests have continued to spread across France amid complaints about school conditions, staffing shortages, class sizes and facilities. AFP reports that more than 5,000 people have been arrested since Monday, while about 735 educational establishments were affected on Friday. Authorities say peaceful protest is permitted but violence will not be tolerated. A further mobilisation is expected on Tuesday.
articles.imageQuery: France student protest school students Paris

articles.title: Nigeria: 20 Prospective NYSC Members Reportedly Abducted in Imo
articles.content: Families of 20 prospective National Youth Service Corps members abducted while travelling from Oyo State to their orientation camps say kidnappers have demanded ₦1 billion in ransom. The victims were travelling along the Owerri–Onitsha Road in Imo State when gunmen attacked two buses. Police say a suspected hideout has been identified, but an immediate operation was delayed because of fears that the area may have been planted with improvised explosive devices. The rescue operation remains ongoing and details may change as authorities provide further information.
articles.imageQuery: Nigeria security police road security operation

articles.title: Ethiopia: Fighting Intensifies Around Tigray Capital
articles.content: Renewed fighting in northern Ethiopia is raising concerns about a wider regional crisis. Reuters reports that Ethiopian federal forces have recaptured Alula Aba Nega Airport in Mekelle, the capital of Tigray, following renewed clashes involving government forces and an alliance led by the Tigray People's Liberation Front. Ethiopia's relations with Eritrea have also deteriorated, while Addis Ababa has accused Eritrea, Sudan and Egypt of supporting opposition forces. Those countries deny the allegations. The African Union has called for restraint.

articles.title: North Korea Confirms Intermediate-Range Missile Test
articles.content: North Korea has confirmed that it conducted an intermediate-range strategic ballistic missile test. South Korea's military said the missile travelled more than 700 kilometres towards the sea off North Korea's east coast. North Korean officials said the weapon incorporated artificial-intelligence-related capabilities, including the ability to adjust its flight path, but those technical claims have not been independently verified. South Korea continues to monitor the security situation.
articles.imageQuery: North Korea missile launch Kim Jong Un

articles.title: Europe Balances Energy Security and Rising Fuel Costs
articles.content: European governments continue to face pressure from elevated energy and refined-fuel prices. The G7 emergency reserve release is intended to increase diesel and crude availability and reduce market pressure. The continuing conflict around Iran and disruptions to global energy infrastructure mean that European households, transport operators and manufacturers remain exposed to changes in fuel costs.
articles.imageQuery: Europe energy crisis fuel petrol station

articles.title: Dangote Refinery Remains Important to Nigeria's Energy Position
articles.content: Nigeria's Dangote Refinery remains a major part of the country's energy and industrial story as global fuel markets face disruption. The refinery's large-scale production capacity has increased Nigeria's ability to supply refined petroleum products domestically and internationally. The Dangote share offering is also attracting considerable attention from Nigerian investors. However, investment in shares carries risk and strong public interest does not guarantee future returns.

articles.title: Global Markets Watch Energy Supply and Emergency Reserves
articles.content: Financial markets are continuing to assess the impact of the Iran conflict, energy supply disruptions and the G7 emergency reserve release. The International Energy Agency says oil prices have begun to fall following the reserve-release announcement. Reuters reported Brent crude settling around $102.25 a barrel on Friday, while WTI settled at about $91.11.
articles.imageQuery: global financial markets oil trading screen

articles.title: Canada Designates Pacific Link Pipeline as Project of National Interest
articles.content: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has designated the proposed West Coast Oil Pipeline, now known as Pacific Link, as a project of national interest. The Canadian government says the project is intended to expand export access to Asian markets and reduce dependence on a single trading partner. The proposal involves Canada and Alberta sharing ownership, with Indigenous communities being offered a minimum 10 percent ownership interest.
articles.imageQuery: Canada oil pipeline Alberta British Columbia

articles.title: Asia Watches North Korean Missile Activity
articles.content: Security concerns remain elevated in East Asia following North Korea's latest ballistic missile test. South Korea and Japan are closely monitoring developments, while Pyongyang continues to describe its strategic weapons programme as part of its national defence and deterrence policy.

morningSummary: The global picture this Sunday is dominated by three interconnected pressures: the unresolved Iran–US confrontation, the resulting energy-security shock and growing domestic security and social pressures in several countries. The G7's 100-million-barrel emergency reserve release is aimed at easing fuel-market pressure, while traffic and oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz remain closely watched. In Europe, France is experiencing major student protests. In Africa, Nigeria is dealing with an ongoing NYSC abduction crisis while renewed fighting in Ethiopia raises regional concerns. In Asia, North Korea's latest missile test adds to existing security tensions.
bigQuestion: As governments respond to war, energy pressure, insecurity and public unrest, how can national leaders protect ordinary people while maintaining long-term economic and social stability?
quoteOfTheDay: A wise society does not measure progress only by the strength of its leaders or the size of its economy, but by the security, opportunities and dignity experienced by ordinary people.
